To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human beings are pattern-seeking, story-telling animals, and we are very good at finding patterns and telling stories, even those that have no basis in fact.
people use a limited number of heuristic principles which reduce the complex tasks of assessing probabilities and predicting values to simpler judgemental operations.
people tend to be overconfident in their judgements and decisions, and to be influenced by the representativeness heuristic, the availability heuristic, and the adjustment and anchoring heuristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cognitive basis of judgment and choice.
the psychology of human reasoning.
the cognitive mechanisms that underlie the way people estimate probabilities and make judgments of likelihood and confidence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heuristics and biases approach is a useful framework for understanding the cognitive processes underlying judgment and decision making.
the heuristics and biases program is one of the most important developments in the field of decision making and problem solving in psychology.
the heuristics and biases are the result of a combination of cognitive and motivational factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heuristics of judgement under uncertainty are fast, efficient, but also often wrong.
the human mind employs simple heuristics to facilitate making judgements under conditions of uncertainty.
people tend to be over-confident, and place too much faith in their intuition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way people think is often quite different from the way they should think.
people are not as rational as we would like to believe.
we are not very good at making judgments under uncertainty.
